content:
At last night's Emmy Awards ceremony, Apple TV+ had an outstanding performance, beating competitors like HBO to become the platform with the most wins that evening. Below is HBO's Casey Bloys' response to Apple TV+'s wins.

HBO's CEO praised Apple TV+'s outstanding performance, while also acknowledging that competing with a company valued at one trillion dollars is "rather a challenge".

Apple TV+ has long been compared to HBO, as both prioritise quality over quantity. Apple is even occasionally referred to as "the new generation HBO".

Last night's Emmy Awards further cemented this notion, with Apple TV+ surpassing HBO, Netflix, and other platforms to become the most awarded platform of the night.

Apple TV+ swept a total of 29 awards, earning the honour of "most awarded network of the year", with shows like 'Widow's Bay' performing particularly well. HBO followed closely behind with 21 awards.

After the Emmy ceremony, HBO executive Casey Bloys spoke with Deadline and was asked for his thoughts on Apple TV+'s performance. Here's what he said:

DEADLINE: What are your thoughts on Apple TV+'s performance this time? They became the most awarded platform at the Emmys for the first time — do you have anything to say? BLOYS: I'm actually really happy about it, because I think they're strong competitors — Zack and Jamie. We've always had strong competitors — Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon — so Apple joining the fray keeps everyone on their toes, and that's exactly when I perform at my best. They're a company valued at one trillion dollars, so it's undoubtedly a big challenge, but we'll continue doing what we've always been doing, which is making the best possible programmes.

Bloys joined HBO in 2004 and has been in charge of programming since 2016. His track record speaks for itself, and his response to Apple TV+'s wins was largely gracious and sincere, offering heartfelt congratulations.

However, the most interesting part of his response was this line: "They're a company valued at one trillion dollars, so it's undoubtedly a big challenge."

We don't know Apple TV+'s internal budget, but it's undeniable that Apple's overall financial resources far exceed those of most competitors, including HBO.

Coincidentally, Paramount is currently actively seeking to acquire HBO (along with other Warner Bros. Discovery assets), hoping to compete more effectively with tech giants like Apple and Amazon.

Does scale naturally bring advantage? Possibly. But many networks have already proven that, when it comes to producing content audiences love, money is only a small part of the equation.

Apple TV+ costs USD 14.99 per month, and can also be purchased as part of the Apple One subscription bundle.
